title: Chronic Myeloid Leukaemia, Polycythaemia Vera, Essential Thrombocythaemia, and Myelofibrosis

steps.tx: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm originating in pluripotent haematopoietic stem cells, driven by the reciprocal translocation t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2). This chromosomal rearrangement produces the Philadelphia chromosome, fusing the breakpoint cluster region gene to ABL1. The resulting p210 oncoprotein encodes a constitutively active **BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase** that drives massive proliferation of the granulocytic series. Peripheral blood displays marked leukocytosis, a low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score, and a full spectrum of maturing myeloid precursors.
steps.say: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is driven by the Philadelphia chromosome, resulting from a translocation between chromosomes nine and twenty-two that generates the constitutively active BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase oncoprotein. This enzyme phosphorylates downstream signalling cascades, causing massive granulocyte proliferation. Peripheral smears characteristically demonstrate prominent leukocytosis with a complete maturation spectrum from myeloblasts to mature neutrophils, accompanied by a characteristically low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase score.

vis.alt: Pathogenesis and blood smear findings in BCR-ABL1 positive chronic myeloid leukaemia
vis.caption: Chronic myeloid leukaemia pathogenesis driven by BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase.

steps.tx: The discovery of selective small-molecule **tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy** transformed chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable chronic condition. Agents including imatinib, dasatinib, and nilotinib compete with adenosine triphosphate for the kinase domain binding pocket of BCR-ABL1, inhibiting substrate phosphorylation and inducing leukemic cell apoptosis. Quantitative real-time reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction monitors treatment response on the International Scale, aiming for a major molecular response defined as BCR-ABL1 transcripts under 0.1 percent.
steps.say: Targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors like imatinib revolutionized chronic myeloid leukaemia management by binding the ATP-binding pocket of the BCR-ABL1 kinase, shutting down aberrant signaling. Patient response is tracked by quantitative reverse transcriptase PCR from peripheral blood. Achieving a major molecular response, defined as a three-log reduction with BCR-ABL1 transcripts below zero point one percent on the International Scale, predicts excellent long-term progression-free survival.

steps.tx: Natural progression of untreated chronic myeloid leukaemia follows three distinct stages: chronic phase, accelerated phase, and terminal blast crisis. **Blast crisis transformation** mimics acute leukaemia, diagnosed when myeloblasts or lymphoblasts constitute twenty percent or more of peripheral blood leukocytes or bone marrow nucleated cells, or when extramedullary blast proliferation occurs. Seventy percent of blast crises evolve into acute myeloid leukaemia, while thirty percent present as acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, conclusively demonstrating the pluripotent stem cell origin of CML.
steps.say: Without effective therapy, chronic myeloid leukaemia advances from its indolent chronic phase through an accelerated phase into blast crisis. Blast crisis is defined by finding twenty percent or more blasts in the blood or marrow, or by developing extramedullary chloromas. Interestingly, seventy percent of blast crises are myeloid while thirty percent are lymphoblastic, confirming that the Philadelphia translocation originates in a primitive pluripotent haematopoietic stem cell.

left.title: Chronic Phase CML
points: Easily controlled with oral daily TKIs

right.title: Blast Crisis Phase CML
points: Requires intensive induction and allogeneic transplant

steps.tx: Polycythaemia vera is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by autonomous overproduction of red blood cells independent of physiological erythropoietin regulation. Patients manifest symptoms of vascular stasis, thrombotic events such as Budd-Chiari hepatic vein thrombosis, and striking **aquagenic pruritus** provoked by warm bathing due to mast cell degranulation. Diagnostic laboratory evaluation reveals elevated haematocrit exceeding forty-nine percent in men or forty-eight percent in women, panmyelosis with leukocytosis and thrombocytosis, and characteristically suppressed serum erythropoietin levels.
steps.say: Polycythaemia vera involves autonomous, unregulated erythropoiesis leading to an expanded red blood cell mass. Blood viscosity rises dramatically, predisposing patients to deep venous and arterial thromboses, including Budd-Chiari syndrome. A classic symptom is aquagenic pruritus, where warm water exposure triggers intense itching from basophil and mast cell histamine release. Markedly low serum erythropoietin with high haematocrit confirms autonomous erythropoiesis.

vis.alt: Polycythaemia vera diagnostic features and complications
vis.caption: Polycythaemia vera with JAK2 driven erythrocytosis and thrombotic risk.

steps.tx: Over ninety-five percent of patients with polycythaemia vera carry the somatic **JAK2 V617F mutation** located in exon 14 of the Janus kinase 2 gene. This point mutation substitutes valine with phenylalanine at codon 617 within the JH2 pseudokinase regulatory domain, abolishing auto-inhibitory control and conferring constitutive tyrosine kinase activation. Intracellular signaling cascades downstream of the erythropoietin receptor, including STAT5, AKT, and MAPK, remain permanently active, driving red blood cell proliferation even in the complete absence of circulating erythropoietin.
steps.say: The somatic JAK2 V617F mutation is present in more than ninety-five percent of polycythaemia vera cases. By replacing valine with phenylalanine at codon six-seventeen in the autoinhibitory pseudokinase domain, this mutation unlocks permanent kinase activity. Downstream STAT5 signaling fires continuously, driving erythroblast proliferation and survival completely independent of erythropoietin binding.

steps.tx: Essential thrombocythaemia is defined by sustained clonal proliferation of the megakaryocytic lineage producing persistent peripheral thrombocytosis exceeding 450,000 per microliter. Bone marrow examination demonstrates marked megakaryocytic hyperplasia characterized by **staghorn giant megakaryocytes** displaying hyperlobated, deeply folded nuclei clustered in loose aggregates without accompanying reticulin fibrosis. Patients paradoxically oscillate between microvascular thrombotic occlusions, such as digital gangrene and transient ischaemic attacks, and mucocutaneous bleeding caused by acquired von Willebrand syndrome at platelet counts exceeding one million.
steps.say: Essential thrombocythaemia is characterized by sustained platelet counts above four hundred and fifty thousand per microliter. Bone marrow trephine biopsies show clusters of giant, hyperlobated megakaryocytes resembling staghorn antlers, without significant fibrosis. While microvascular thrombosis and erythromelalgia are common, extreme thrombocytosis above one million platelets per microliter paradoxically causes mucocutaneous bleeding due to acquired von Willebrand factor consumption.

vis.alt: Peripheral blood and bone marrow histology in essential thrombocythaemia
vis.caption: Essential thrombocythaemia overview with sustained thrombocytosis and thrombotic risk.

steps.tx: Primary myelofibrosis is a clonal stem cell neoplasm in which malignant megakaryocytes secrete excess platelet-derived growth factor and transforming growth factor-beta into the marrow stroma. These fibrogenic cytokines stimulate non-clonal reactive fibroblasts to deposit extensive collagen and reticulin meshworks, causing progressive bone marrow obliteration. Displaced haematopoietic stem cells migrate into the spleen and liver, establishing extensive **extramedullary haematopoiesis** that culminates in massive, symptomatic splenomegaly, severe portal hypertension, and debilitating constitutional cachexia.
steps.say: In primary myelofibrosis, clonal megakaryocytes release fibrogenic cytokines, principally PDGF and TGF-beta, stimulating polyclonal fibroblasts to deposit dense collagen throughout the marrow space. As marrow space is obliterated, haematopoiesis escapes to extramedullary sanctuaries in the spleen and liver. Patients present with massive splenomegaly, splenic infarction pain, profound fatigue, and constitutional wasting.

left.title: Primary Myelofibrosis
points: Median survival 5 to 7 years without transplant

right.title: Essential Thrombocythaemia
points: Normal red cell and white cell morphology
Near-normal life expectancy with antiplatelet therapy

steps.tx: Extensive stromal collagen deposition in primary myelofibrosis obliterates sinusoidal vascular beds, routinely resulting in a **dry tap on bone marrow aspiration**. Establishing the diagnosis necessitates a trephine core biopsy stained with Gomori silver impregnation to evaluate reticulin fibrosis grade. Peripheral blood examination reveals a classic leucoerythroblastic picture characterized by circulating immature myeloid precursors, nucleated red blood cells, and numerous teardrop poikilocytes (dacrocytes) deformed while squeezing across rigid fibrotic splenic sinusoids.
steps.say: Dense stromal fibrosis prevents aspirating liquid marrow, resulting in a classic dry tap that mandates a bone marrow trephine core biopsy. Silver reticulin staining highlights extensive intersecting collagen fibers. The peripheral smear shows a classic leucoerythroblastic picture with myelocytes, nucleated red blood cells, and pathognomonic teardrop poikilocytes deformed as they squeeze out of fibrotic marrow and splenic cords.

quiz.q: Which molecular abnormality is present in over 95% of patients diagnosed with polycythaemia vera?
options: JAK2 V617F point mutation in exon 14
quiz.explain: The somatic JAK2 V617F mutation in the JH2 pseudokinase domain occurs in >95% of polycythaemia vera cases, producing constitutively active kinase signaling.

quiz.q: What morphological finding on peripheral blood film is characteristic of primary myelofibrosis?
quiz.explain: Primary myelofibrosis produces a leucoerythroblastic blood picture with teardrop poikilocytes (dacrocytes) caused by distorted release through fibrotic marrow and splenic cords.

quiz.q: What blast percentage threshold in the blood or bone marrow defines blast crisis in chronic myeloid leukaemia?
quiz.explain: Blast crisis in CML is diagnosed when blasts constitute 20% or more of peripheral blood white cells or bone marrow nucleated cells, or upon finding extramedullary blast proliferation.
